candidateDecisions.label: Modern and contemporary art and architecture

analysis: The broad plan builds direct art history and visual analysis from Renaissance to contemporary work, material evidence through world and Greek archaeology, non-European object study through African Art & Heritage, museum display and art historiography. Ancient heritage, historical inquiry, literature and qualitative research support interpretation without standing in for architectural survey or field training. The earlier-art plan retains Renaissance architecture and Mediterranean exchange, Greek material culture, ancient heritage and historical source work. Introduction to Literary Studies brings close reading of narratives that inform older objects, and Introduction to Western Philosophy develops historical intellectual context. These replace nineteenth-century-and-later gender and Native American history courses in the earlier-art option only. Contemporary museum, media and American historical work remains complementary rather than central to that option. The modern plan develops modern art and museums, photographic and film representation, documentary production, environmental media and sociological analysis of publics. It remains a related visual-culture response with partial architectural overlap. Pairwise differences are five, eight and twelve courses (37.5, 60 and 90 EC). Both specialist directions sustain their own emphasis, and the schedules all meet the 24-course and advanced-level requirements. The separate Utrecht thesis and UCR independent research element are explicit. No dedicated art conservation, architecture sequence or equivalent field excursion is claimed.

alignment.rationale: UCR develops academic writing and source evaluation. Utrecht introduces research methods specific to art history.
Both introduce visual interpretation and Western art history. UCR starts with late-medieval and Renaissance art.
Both use material evidence to interpret cultural objects. UCR approaches objects through archaeology.
UCR studies Renaissance painting, sculpture and architecture in a Mediterranean context.
UCR studies African art and heritage through objects and their contexts. Utrecht develops an art-historical research project on exchange.
Both study modern art. UCR examines how museums display and interpret it.
Both examine how heritage is interpreted and used. UCR focuses on ancient democracy and its material legacy.
Both examine methods, historiography and writing in art history.
Utrecht has a dedicated course in late-antique and medieval art. UCR offers related material in broader courses.
Utrecht studies architecture from objects and buildings to urban space.
Utrecht has a dedicated course on earlier architecture. UCR addresses buildings within art history and archaeology.
Utrecht includes an excursion focused on earlier art and architecture.
UCR considers global perspectives across several courses. Utrecht includes a dedicated global art history course.
UCR studies myths and narratives that can inform interpretation of images. Utrecht teaches iconography as a distinct method.

Utrecht requires an individual 15 EC art history thesis after at least 15 EC at advanced level. UCR develops source-based research in a history seminar and offers separate optional independent research.
Utrecht students choose 60 EC of profiling, including a coherent 30 EC package and at least 15 EC at intermediate or advanced level.
